newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S BRM RESCHEDULES 25,000T SCRAP TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S BRM RESCHEDULES 25,000T SCRAP TENDER.

text.p: Romania's Bucharest-based commodities exchange has rescheduled for October 11 a tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron, the exchange said on Thursday.

Bursa Romana de Marfuri (BRM) said in a statment it had rescheduled the tender initially announced for September 25 as "none of the bidders has complied with the requirements of the tender documents." It gave no details.
The minimum starting price for a tonne of iron scrap offered in the international tender scheduled for October 11 had been maintained at $95, BRM said.
Bidders have until October 10 to submit offers.
The scrap cames from old rolling stock. Till mid-1996, Romania applied a full ban on scrap iron exports.
But in July, the Balkan country set an export quota for scrap iron of 100,000 tonnes this year with plans to fully liberalise export of the commodity by 1998.
Scrap iron from the shipping sector and rolling stock would make the bulk of those exports, the industry ministry said.
Liberalisation of scrap iron exports is part of Romania's strategy to adapt its legislation to that of the EU internal market, in view of its possible membership.
